name: JusPrin nightly

# Builds jusprin-dev, the development branch, once a day and puts the files
# on the "nightly-builds" pre-release, replacing the day before's, as
# JusPrin 1's "Build all" did.
#
# - GitHub runs scheduled workflows only on the default branch, main. The
#   scheduled run therefore only starts this workflow again on jusprin-dev,
#   so every step, OrcaSlicer's dependency build included, checks out
#   jusprin-dev.
# - The build is the release's (jusprin_build_all.yml), so a nightly is what a
#   release from the same commit would be. Its version is the one in
#   src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Updates/Version.hpp.
# - The files keep JusPrin 1's nightly names, so download links stay the
#   same: JusPrin_Windows_Installer_nightly.exe,
#   JusPrin_Windows_nightly_portable.zip, JusPrin_Mac_universal_nightly.dmg,
#   JusPrin_Linux_AppImage_Ubuntu2404_nightly.AppImage, and SHA256SUMS.txt.
# - The nightly-builds tag moves to the commit built, and the release notes
#   name it. The scheduled build is skipped when jusprin-dev has not changed
#   since the last nightly.
# - The macOS app is signed and notarised; Windows builds are unsigned.
# - The app's update check never offers a nightly: it reads only tags named
#   vX.Y.Z and jusprin/vX.Y.Z (ReleaseFeed.cpp).
# - GitHub's hosted Apple-silicon macOS runners are often all taken in US
#   daytime, and GitHub cancels a job that gets none within 15 minutes. The
#   scheduled run lands in those hours, because this repo's schedules start
#   hours late. A run whose only failures are such jobs starts the nightly
#   again, up to 8 runs a day for one commit.
#
# Run it by hand from Actions > JusPrin nightly > Run workflow, with the
# branch set to jusprin-dev.

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '35 7 * * *' # near midnight US Pacific time, as JusPrin 1's nightly
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      sign_macos:
        description: 'Sign and notarise the macOS app with the Apple secrets'
        type: boolean

1	---
2	name: jusprin-release
3	description: Use when asked to make, prepare or start a new JusPrin release (a new version on GitHub), from choosing the commit range to the after-publish steps. Covers the version, release notes, server readiness, translations, the error-handling audit, tests, the guide check, moving main, the release workflow, testing the draft and what follows publishing. Not for JusPrin 1 (jusprin-v1) or OrcaSlicer's own releases.
4	---
5	
6	# Making a JusPrin release
7	
8	The release workflow, `.github/workflows/jusprin_release.yml`, builds the
9	release files from one commit and uploads them to a draft release on GitHub.
10	It refuses the commit without a new version, release notes and a guide check
11	(see "Releasing" in `AGENTS.md`). It does not run the test suites, check the
12	server, check the translations or audit error handling. This skill covers
13	those too, in the order they have to happen.
14	
15	## Kenneth decides these
16	
17	Ask Kenneth, in plain words, and wait for his yes before each of these. A yes
18	covers that one action, not the next one.
19	
20	- The version number, when he has not named it.
21	- The release notes' wording. Show him the file.
22	- Deploying the server.
23	- Spending API money on live AI checks. Say the cost.
24	- Pushing to `jusprin-dev`, and moving `main` forward.
25	- Starting the release workflow.
26	- Downloading the draft's files to this computer.
27	- Posting anything on GitHub, such as replies to issues.
28	
29	**Never publish the draft.** Kenneth publishes it by hand on the Releases page.
30	Never force-push `main`.
31	
32	## 1. Set up
33	
34	1. Check that the main checkout (the folder that holds `jusprin-dev`, not a
35	   worktree) has nothing that would be left out of the release:
36	
37	   ```bash
38	   git -C <main checkout> fetch origin
39	   git -C <main checkout> status --porcelain -uno
40	   git -C <main checkout> log --oneline origin/jusprin-dev..jusprin-dev
41	   ```
42	
43	   Both must print nothing. A changed file or a commit that is not on GitHub
44	   is work someone may expect in the release. Stop, list each one for
45	   Kenneth, and wait until he has pushed it or said to leave it out. Do not
46	   push, commit or discard it yourself. Untracked files do not block: they
47	   are working docs Kenneth keeps there on purpose.
48	2. Find the last release: `git tag --list 'jusprin/v*' --sort=-v:refname | head -1`.
49	   The range is that tag to `origin/jusprin-dev` (after `git fetch origin`).
50	3. Make your own worktree from `origin/jusprin-dev`, under
51	   `<repo>/.claude/worktrees/`, on a branch named `claude/release-<version>`.
52	   Never name it `jusprin-release/...`: pushing a branch with that name starts
53	   an unsigned release build.
54	4. Read every commit in the range: `git log --format='%h %s%n%b' <range>`.
55	   Note what a person would notice, and the GitHub issues each change fixes.
56	
57	## 2. Version and release notes
58

# usage: python3 -I standin.py <port> <launch-status> <log-file>
# One local stand-in for both JusPrin's server and Sentry. Records every
# request (method, path, headers that matter, body) as one JSON line;
# answers POST /ent/jusprin/v2/launches with <launch-status>, a Sentry
# envelope POST (/api/<project>/envelope/) with 200 and its event id, and
# everything else with 404.
import json, sys
from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, ThreadingHTTPServer

port, launch_status, log_path = int(sys.argv[1]), int(sys.argv[2]), sys.argv[3]


class Handler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    def _answer(self):
        length = int(self.headers.get("Content-Length") or 0)
        raw = self.rfile.read(length) if length else b""
        if self.headers.get("Transfer-Encoding", "").lower() == "chunked":
            chunks = []
            while True:
                size = int(self.rfile.readline().strip(), 16)
                if size == 0:
                    self.rfile.readline(); break
                chunks.append(self.rfile.read(size)); self.rfile.readline()
            raw = b"".join(chunks)
        record = {"method": self.command, "path": self.path, "headers": dict(self.headers.items()), "length": len(raw)}
        if "/minidump/" in self.path:
            # A crash: crashpad's multipart upload, gzipped; kept as it came.
            record["body_file"] = f"{log_path}.{self.path.split('guid=')[-1][:36]}.bin"
            open(record["body_file"], "wb").write(raw)
            body = ""
        else:
            body = raw.decode("utf-8", "replace")
        record["body"] = body
        with open(log_path, "a") as log:
            log.write(json.dumps(record) + "\n")
        if self.path.startswith("/ent/jusprin/v2/launches"):
            status, text = launch_status, '{"detail": "stand-in server fault"}'
        elif "/minidump/" in self.path:
            status, text = 200, '{"id": "00000000000000000000000000000000"}'
        elif "/envelope/" in self.path:
            status, text = 200, json.dumps({"id": json.loads(body.split("\n")[0]).get("event_id")})
        else:
            status, text = 404, '{"detail": "not here"}'
        data = text.encode()
        self.send_response(status)
        self.send_header("Content-Type", "application/json")
        self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(data)))
        self.end_headers()
        self.wfile.write(data)

    do_GET = do_POST = do_PUT = do_DELETE = _answer

    def log_message(self, *args):
        pass


ThreadingHTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", port), Handler).serve_forever()

content.text:
The app and its pages no longer trim anything the Sentry libraries gather, and every report and crash now also carries this run's log file. Every release and nightly build now uploads its debug files and fails unless Sentry ends up holding function names for the app's code. Nothing is committed.

**What changed in the app**
- I removed every piece of trimming I had added. Events now keep the install id as `user` and the home folder in paths, and the server is no longer told not to store IP addresses. Session updates are sent again, and page console lines and full click details are kept.
- Two older pieces of code, which predate this work, still put `~` in place of the home folder and cut long lines in the report's own text. Tell me if those should go too.
- **The "Report to JusPrin team" button** sends the same full report as automatic mode: stack, modules, breadcrumbs and log. Nothing about it was hard.
- **Crashes with automatic reports off** are never sent. The minidump stays in the app's data folder and isn't sent later, even after automatic reports are turned on. I don't think that needs a choice.

**Tested on this Mac, against the local stand-in**
- **App failure, reports on:** one event with the install id, 32 stack frames, 1,060 modules and the 651 KB log file. The log contains the home folder path.
- **Crash, reports on:** the minidump went out with its breadcrumbs, the event and the log.
- **Crash, reports off:** nothing at all went out.
- **Tests:** all suites pass and clang-tidy is clean.
- **Not yet run:** a page error with reports on, and the Report press with reports off. The screen is locked, and pages run no script while it is. A watcher runs both once the screen unlocks.

**Release path**
- The release workflow refuses to start without five repository secrets. Kenneth adds them under Settings › Secrets and variables › Actions:
  - `JUSPRIN_SENTRY_DSN`: the project's client key address;
  - `SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN`: a token allowed project:read and project:write;
  - `SENTRY_URL`;
  - `SENTRY_ORG` = `sentry`;
  - `SENTRY_PROJECT` = `jusprin-app`.
- The nightly build fails without them too, until they are added.
- Each platform's build uploads its debug files with a new script, `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Packaging/sentry_debug_files.sh`. It then fails unless Sentry holds function names for the app's own code, for both Mac architectures.
- The release skill now has three Sentry steps: check the secrets before starting, run the script's check on the draft's files, and look at real events after publishing.
- I pinned sentry-cli to 2.58.6, because 3.x officially supports only self-hosted Sentry 24.11.1 and newer, and this server is 23.1.1.
- **Tested locally:** the script's failure paths, and its debug-id lookup against the real server, read-only. **Only a real release run will show** the upload itself and the Windows and Linux builds.

**Decision needed: the sentences people read.** Each of these is now untrue:
- In the report dialog:
  - "The report is anonymous: it has no chat messages, no files and nothing that says who you are."
  - "Each report holds only the lines under ‘See what the report contains’."
  - "That is the whole report. It has no chat messages, no files, no project names and no account or email address."
- In Preferences, "JusPrin’s server sees your IP address": it is now the Sentry server.

Reports now carry a file (the log), an install id, the home folder path, breadcrumbs, and, for crashes, a memory snapshot holding the launching environment. A server rule removes data only after it has left the computer. So you choose: approve new wording, or accept these sentences as they are. I haven't checked the privacy policy. Which do you want?

**Decision needed: server settings.** The project already has its data scrubber on with the default rules. It also doesn't keep minidumps after the server has worked out the stack. I propose one change: a rule that replaces the user name in home-folder paths, across all event fields and the log attachment. Whether 23.1.1 can apply rules to attachments is my expectation, not checked. I'd change nothing about IP addresses, as you said earlier. May I add that rule?

content.text:
Both page checks passed on this Mac, against the local stand-in. Every case in the plan has now been tested there.

**Why the release needs `SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN`:** the client key in `JUSPRIN_SENTRY_DSN` can only send new events. Uploading each build's debug files needs a login to Sentry's API with project:write; that upload is what lets Sentry turn crash addresses into function names. The release's check that Sentry really holds those names needs project:read. Without the token, reports still arrive, but the C++ stacks show bare addresses.

**Page error with automatic reports on:** one event arrived with the page's stack and six breadcrumbs. The breadcrumbs were the page's console line and the page's message steps. The event also carried the install id as `user`, the app's 1,070 native modules, and the log file (665 KB) as an attachment.

**Automatic reports off, then "Report to JusPrin team" pressed:** until the press, nothing was sent apart from the app's anonymous start message. After it, the same full event and the log went out once, along with Sentry's session updates. So the one-off send carries the full context, as Kenneth wanted.

The first attempts sent nothing because of the test setup, not the app. WebKit served its cached copy of an older test page, which threw its error before the page's Sentry catcher had started. The test page now gets a new file name on every run.

Windows and Linux are still unbuilt and untested, and nothing is committed. The two decisions for Kenneth still stand: new wording for the dialog and Preferences sentences that are now untrue, and the proposed server rule that replaces user names in home-folder paths.

His answer, in full: "Yes, send them". His measure is the one he gave before: "We want the Sentry server to capture as much info as possible so that we can do production troubleshooting."

1. A non-crash report's stack shows where the report was made, not where the failure happened.
   What I did: I took the event recorded in your trial run `p3-on-launch500` and named its frame addresses with `atos`. The stack runs main → Slic3r::CLI::run → GUI_Run → wxEntry → … → wxAsyncMethodCallEventFunctor<report_if_automatic…> → report_if_automatic → sentry_send → sentry_event_value_add_stacktrace → sentry_value_new_stacktrace. It comes from the `sentry_event_value_add_stacktrace(event, nullptr, 0)` call in `sentry_send`, which captures the current thread at the moment of sending.
   Why it matters: AGENTS.md says an unexpected failure is thrown and travels up unchanged to one handler at the top of each entry point. So for nearly every report the useful stack is the one at the throw, and the report has only the handler's (or, after the Report button, the dialog's).
   What is wanted: the report carries the stack of the place the failure was thrown, for exceptions the app throws itself and for ones thrown by libraries (std, boost, wx) where that is possible. Check what the libraries already in the build offer before writing anything of your own, and say what you chose and what it cannot cover. Crash reports are not affected.
   Done looks like: a trial run where a failure is thrown several calls deep, and the recorded event's stack, named with `atos`, shows the throwing function.

2. Mac and Linux release stacks will have function names but no file and line.
   This is my reading of the build scripts, not a run: `build_release_macos.sh` and `build_linux.sh -srlL` build `Release` with no debug information, and the `verify` step of `sentry_debug_files.sh` passes when Sentry holds a file with feature `symtab` alone. Windows passes `/Zi`.
   What is wanted: release builds on all three platforms produce line-level debug information, the release workflow uploads it, the shipped app stays stripped, and `verify` fails unless Sentry holds a file with the `debug` feature for each build id. A memory note here says the app's GUI static library goes over the 4 GiB limit of `ar` once debug information is on and needs `llvm-ar`; I have not re-checked that, so measure it.
   Done looks like: on this Mac, a release-style build whose recorded event resolves to file and line when symbolicated from the debug file you would upload. Say plainly what stays untested for Linux and Windows.

3. Page stacks will be unreadable.
   Also from reading: neither `AgentUI` nor `HomeUI` `vite.config.ts` turns source maps on, and nothing uploads them, so a page error's stack is positions in a minified file.
   What is wanted: the release workflow builds source maps for both pages and uploads them for the release, with a check that fails the release when they are missing, the same way the debug-file check does. The Sentry server is version 23.1.1; check which way of matching maps to frames that version supports before choosing one (I have not checked). Mind what the frame's file name looks like when the page is loaded from the app's own resources.
   Done looks like: a page error's recorded event, and proof that the uploaded map resolves its top frame to the source file and line.

Limits that still hold: no filtering or trimming code in the app; send nothing to the real Sentry projects and change no Sentry setting without Kenneth's word; commit and push nothing; one build per build directory with `-- -j4`, after checking `uptime` and `pgrep -fl ninja`; update the release skill and the "Releasing" section of AGENTS.md if the release steps change. def fetch_release_file(filename, release, dist=None):
    """
    Attempt to retrieve a release artifact from the database.

    Caches the result of that attempt (whether successful or not).
    """
    dist_name = dist and dist.name or None
    cache_key, cache_key_meta = get_cache_keys(filename, release, dist)

    logger.debug("Checking cache for release artifact %r (release_id=%s)", filename, release.id)
    result = cache.get(cache_key)

    # not in the cache (meaning we haven't checked the database recently), so check the database
    if result is None:
        with metrics.timer("sourcemaps.release_artifact_from_file"):
            filename_choices = ReleaseFile.normalize(filename)
            filename_idents = [ReleaseFile.get_ident(f, dist_name) for f in filename_choices]

            logger.debug(
                "Checking database for release artifact %r (release_id=%s)", filename, release.id
            )

            possible_files = list(
                ReleaseFile.objects.filter(
                    release_id=release.id,
                    dist_id=dist.id if dist else dist,
                    ident__in=filename_idents,
                ).select_related("file")
            )

            if len(possible_files) == 0:
                logger.debug(
                    "Release artifact %r not found in database (release_id=%s)",
                    filename,
                    release.id,
                )
                cache.set(cache_key, -1, 60)
                return None

            elif len(possible_files) == 1:
                releasefile = possible_files[0]

            else:
                # Pick first one that matches in priority order.
                # This is O(N*M) but there are only ever at most 4 things here
                # so not really worth optimizing.
                releasefile = next(
                    rf for ident in filename_idents for rf in possible_files if rf.ident == ident
                )

            logger.debug(
                "Found release artifact %r (id=%s, release_id=%s)",
                filename,
                releasefile.id,
                release.id,
            )

            with sentry_sdk.start_span(
                op="JavaScriptStacktraceProcessor.fetch_release_file.fetch_and_cache"
            ):
                result = fetch_and_cache_artifact(
                    filename,
                    lambda: ReleaseFile.cache.getfile(releasefile),
                    cache_key,
                    cache_key_meta,
                    releasefile.file.headers,
                    compress_file,
                )

    # in the cache as an unsuccessful attempt
    elif result == -1:
        result = None

    # in the cache as a successful attempt, including the zipped contents of the file
    else:
        result = result_from_cache(filename, result)

    return result

On 2026-09-13, at jusprin-newui 770bd2b0a2 (after "Add the evidence-led Add a
printer flow"), a worktree RelWithDebInfo build failed archiving
`src/slic3r/RelWithDebInfo/liblibslic3r_gui.a`:
`Assertion failed: (memberOffset < 0xFFFFFFFF) ... ArchiveWriter.cpp` then
`fatal error in .../ranlib`. The archive llvm-ar produced was 4,309,350,176
bytes; the main checkout's copy built minutes earlier was 4,143,827,796 and
still fit. Objects are big because the root CMakeLists.txt (lines ~544-548)
rewrites RelWithDebInfo -O2 to -O0 on purpose. Disk space was not the cause.

**Why:** the failed build left the OLD harness binary in place, and the harness
runs afterwards "passed" against stale code (a new `--printer-setup` flag
silently ran the default mode: same 285 check count). Gate runs on build
success and compare binary mtime.

**How to apply:**
- `-DCMAKE_AR=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar` on an existing build dir does
  nothing: `CMakeFiles/<ver>/CMakeCXXCompiler.cmake` sets CMAKE_AR as a normal
  variable that shadows the cache.
- Working relink: `ninja -f build-RelWithDebInfo.ninja -t commands <target>`,
  drop compile lines, swap ar/ranlib for llvm-ar/llvm-ranlib on the gui archive
  line only, then run EACH line in its own `(cd build/arm64 && eval "$line")`.
  One `sh` script fails with bogus "no such file" errors because the
  encoding-check line does `cd src/slic3r` and it leaks; `sh -e` also does not
  stop inside `&&` chains. Apple's linker accepted the >4 GiB llvm-ar archive.
- The fix is PER BUILD DIRECTORY, nothing in the repo selects llvm-ar. Main
  checkout's build/arm64 cache has llvm-ar (commit 449b676145 documents it in
  agent-docs/macos-build-troubleshooting.md); any newly configured build dir
  gets Apple ar and fails again. Configure new dirs with the flags in
  [[jusprin-worktree-build]].
- Recurred 2026-09-14 on a fresh worktree at jusprin-newui bc19661a7f (archive
  4,308,513,464 bytes). Shortcut that worked: after the failed build, from
  `-t commands shell_integration_harness` drop lines containing ` -c `; only
  the last two remain relevant (gui archive, then harness link). Run just
  those two, swapping ar/ranlib on the archive line. Harness then passed.
- A lasting fix (llvm-ar in the toolchain, thin archives, or less debug info)
  is Kenneth's call; the main checkout will hit this on its next growth.

A JusPrin git worktree builds against the already-built deps by configuring:

```
cmake -B build/arm64 -G "Ninja Multi-Config" -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DCMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES=arm64 -DCMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=15.0 \
  -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH=/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local \
  -DSLIC3R_GUI=ON -DSLIC3R_STATIC=ON -DSLIC3R_PCH=ON -DBUILD_TESTS=ON \
  -DCMAKE_AR=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar -DCMAKE_RANLIB=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ranlib
```

ONE PREFIX PATH (2026-11-15): since the 2.5.0 merge, CMakeLists.txt finds its bundled Python under CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH + /libpython; a two-entry list fails configure with "Bundled Python executable not found under <a;b>/libpython/bin". Pass only the JusPrin deps path (as other worktrees' caches do).

CMAKE BINARY (2026-09-29): configure with `/Applications/CMake.app/Contents/bin/cmake` (put it first on PATH). Homebrew's cmake 4.1 at /opt/homebrew/bin fails with "Could NOT find Eigen3 (missing: EIGEN3_VERSION_OK) (Required is at least version 5.0.1)", and a failed configure poisons the cache: `rm -rf build` before retrying.

The two `CMAKE_AR`/`CMAKE_RANLIB` flags are required on a FRESH build dir:
without them Apple's ar is used and liblibslic3r_gui.a (>4 GiB in
RelWithDebInfo) fails to archive. They only work at first configure, not on
reconfigure. Full story: agent-docs/macos-build-troubleshooting.md. See
[[liblibslic3r-gui-4gib-ar-limit]].

- the URL;
- the URL without its query;

      # macOS: each architecture is built here; jusprin_release.yml joins them

      - name: Prepare the Mac
        if: runner.os == 'macOS'
        run: |
          brew install libtool

          # As OrcaSlicer's build_orca.yml does, for disk space: keep only the
          # selected Xcode.
          xcode=$(basename "$(cd "$(xcode-select -p)/../.." && pwd -P)")
          sudo find /Applications -maxdepth 1 -type d -name "Xcode_*.app" ! -name "$xcode" -exec rm -rf {} +
          sudo rm -rf ~/Library/Developer/CoreSimulator/Caches/*

      - name: Build
        if: runner.os == 'macOS'
        run: ./build_release_macos.sh -s -n -x -j 3 -a ${{ inputs.arch }} -t 10.15

      - name: Package
        if: runner.os == 'macOS'
        run: |
          mkdir -p dist
          tar -czf "dist/JusPrin_Mac_bundle_${{ inputs.arch }}.tar.gz" -C "build/${{ inputs.arch }}" OrcaSlicer

      # Linux
      - name: Install the build packages
        if: runner.os == 'Linux'
        uses: ./.github/actions/apt-install-deps

      - name: Build
        if: runner.os == 'Linux'
        run: |
          # -s builds the slicer and lays out build/package; JusPrin's AppImage
          # replaces OrcaSlicer's (-i).
          ./build_linux.sh -srlL
          ./scripts/check_appimage_libs.sh ./build/package ./build/package/bin/orca-slicer

      - name: Package
        if: runner.os == 'Linux'
        run: |
          ./src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Packaging/appimage.sh build/package "$VERSION" \
            "dist/JusPrin_Linux_AppImage_Ubuntu2404_V${VERSION}${{ inputs.arch && format('_{0}', inputs.arch) || '' }}.AppImage"

      # What lets Sentry name the functions in a crash or a report's stack: each
      # executable and library the app ships, with its PDB on Windows, filed by
      # its build id. The build fails unless Sentry then holds names for the
      # app's own code (Packaging/sentry_debug_files.sh). Sentry's address and
      # the token that may upload stay in the repository's secrets.
      - name: Upload debug files to Sentry
        shell: bash
        env:
          SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN }}
          SENTRY_URL: ${{ secrets.SENTRY_URL }}
          SENTRY_ORG: ${{ secrets.SENTRY_ORG }}
          SENTRY_PROJECT: ${{ secrets.SENTRY_PROJECT }}
        run: |
          case "$RUNNER_OS" in
            Windows) main=build/src/Release/OrcaSlicer.dll; paths=(build/OrcaSlicer build/src/Release) ;;
            macOS)
              app="build/${{ inputs.arch }}/OrcaSlicer/OrcaSlicer.app"
              main="$app/Contents/MacOS/OrcaSlicer"; paths=("$app/Contents") ;;
            *) main=build/package/bin/orca-slicer; paths=(build/package/bin build/package/lib) ;;
          esac
          ./src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Packaging/sentry_debug_files.sh upload "$main" "${paths[@]}"

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: jusprin-${{ runner.os }}-${{ inputs.arch || 'x64' }}
          path: dist/*
          if-no-files-found: error

envelopes through `window.__jusprinBridge.deliver(envelope)` (`WebShared/bridgeClient.ts`).

`assistant_started` with no `assistant_delta` to freeze a streaming empty turn,
`printer_session` to pin a card, `printer_added` for Home's receipt strip. A file

proof. It proves page rendering only; host behaviour (e.g. the 256 KiB image

content.text: Writing the upload-and-check script for the page maps, using Sentry 23.1.1's release-files API directly.

input.content:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Gives Sentry what it needs to name the Agent and Home pages' own code in a
# page error's stack: each page's index.html and its source map
# (WebShared/inlinedScriptSourceMap.ts), filed under the app's release and the
# page's build (WebShared/errorReports.ts), at the names the page's frames
# carry: app:///agent/index.html and app:///home/index.html.
#
#   sentry_page_maps.sh upload
#       Run after a build, from the repository's top folder. Files this
#       build's pages and maps under JUSPRIN_PAGE_BUILD, the build the pages
#       were built with, then verifies them. A file Sentry already holds for
#       that build must be the same file; another platform's build of the same
#       commit uploads the same pages.
#   sentry_page_maps.sh verify [<resources folder>]
#       Fails unless Sentry holds, for this version, exactly these index.html
#       files (by content) and a source map beside each. <resources folder> is
#       the one that holds jusprin/agent and jusprin/home, by default the
#       repository's; the release skill passes a released app's.
#
# Reads SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN, SENTRY_URL, SENTRY_ORG and SENTRY_PROJECT, and
# fails without any of them. Sentry 23.1.1 finds a page's map by its frames'
# file name, release and dist only; it has no debug ids for JavaScript.
set -euo pipefail

top=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/../../../../.." && pwd)

missing=()
for name in SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN SENTRY_URL SENTRY_ORG SENTRY_PROJECT; do
    [ -n "${!name:-}" ] || missing+=("$name")
done
if [ ${#missing[@]} -gt 0 ]; then
    echo "::error::Sentry cannot get the pages' source maps without the secret(s) ${missing[*]}; page error reports from this build would not name the pages' code."
    exit 1
fi

command=${1:-}
if [ "$command" != upload ] && [ "$command" != verify ]; then
    echo "usage: $0 upload | verify [<resources folder>]" >&2
    exit 2
fi
resources=${2:-$top/resources}

# The release the app's events carry (Updates/Version.hpp version_label()).
version=$(sed -n 's/.*kVersion\[\] = "\(.*\)";.*/\1/p' "$top/src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Updates/Version.hpp")
orca=$(sed -n 's/^set(SoftFever_VERSION "\(.*\)")/\1/p' "$top/version.inc")
release="JusPrin $version (OrcaSlicer $orca)"
encoded=$(node -e 'console.log(encodeURIComponent(process.argv[1]))' "$release")
api="${SENTRY_URL%/}/api/0"
files_api="$api/projects/$SENTRY_ORG/$SENTRY_PROJECT/releases/$encoded/files/"
auth=(-H "Authorization: Bearer $SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN")

page_html() { printf '%s/jusprin/%s/index.html' "$resources" "$1"; }
page_map() {
    case "$1" in
        agent) printf '%s/src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/dist/index.html.map' "$top" ;;
        home) printf '%s/src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/HomeUI/dist/index.html.map' "$top" ;;
    esac
}
sha1_of() { shasum -a 1 "$1" | cut -d' ' -f1; }

# Every file Sentry holds for the release, one "<name>\t<dist>\t<sha1>\t<Sourcemap header>" per line.
held_files() {
    local cursor="" page
    while :; do
        page=$(curl -fsS -D /dev/stderr "${auth[@]}" "$files_api?per_page=100${cursor:+&cursor=$cursor}" 2>"$headers_file") || return 1
        printf '%s' "$page" | node -e 'let s="";process.stdin.on("data",d=>s+=d).on("end",()=>{for(const f of JSON.parse(s))console.log([f.name,f.dist??"",f.sha1,(f.headers||{}).Sourcemap??""].join("\t"))})'
        cursor=$(grep -i '^link:' "$headers_file" | sed -n 's/.*rel="next"; results="true"; cursor="\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p')
        [ -n "$cursor" ] || return 0
    done
}
headers_file=$(mktemp)
trap 'rm -f "$headers_file"' EXIT

if [ "$command" = upload ]; then
    build=${JUSPRIN_PAGE_BUILD:-}
    if [ -z "$build" ]; then
        echo "::error::JUSPRIN_PAGE_BUILD names no build, so the pages carry none and Sentry could not tell their maps from another build's."
        exit 1
    fi
    for page in agent home; do
        for file in "$(page_html $page)" "$(page_map $page)"; do
            [ -f "$file" ] || { echo "::error::$file does not exist."; exit 1; }
        done
        grep -q "\"$build\"" "$(page_html $page)" || {
            echo "::error::$(page_html $page) was not built with JUSPRIN_PAGE_BUILD=$build."
            exit 1
        }
    done
    # An existing release answers 208; either way it is there afterwards.
    curl -fsS -o /dev/null "${auth[@]}" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
        -d "$(node -e 'console.log(JSON.stringify({version:process.argv[1],projects:[process.argv[2]]}))' "$release" "$SENTRY_PROJECT")" \
        "$api/organizations/$SENTRY_ORG/releases/"
    held=$(held_files)
    for page in agent home; do
        for kind in html map; do
            if [ $kind = html ]; then file=$(page_html $page); name="app:///$page/index.html"; header=(-F "header=Sourcemap:index.html.map")
            else file=$(page_map $page); name="app:///$page/index.html.map"; header=(); fi
            sha=$(sha1_of "$file")
            existing=$(printf '%s\n' "$held" | awk -F'\t' -v n="$name" -v d="$build" '$1==n && $2==d {print $3}')
            if [ -n "$existing" ]; then
                [ "$existing" = "$sha" ] || {
                    echo "::error::Sentry already holds a different $name for build $build; this platform's page differs from another's of the same commit, and one map cannot serve both."
                    exit 1
                }
                echo "Sentry already holds this $name for build $build."
                continue
            fi
            curl -fsS -o /dev/null "${auth[@]}" -F "file=@$file" -F "name=$name" -F "dist=$build" "${header[@]}" "$files_api" || {
                # Another platform's job may have filed it a moment ago.
                again=$(held_files | awk -F'\t' -v n="$name" -v d="$build" '$1==n && $2==d {print $3}')
                [ "$again" = "$sha" ] || { echo "::error::Sentry refused $name for build $build."; exit 1; }
            }
            echo "Filed $name for build $build."
        done
    done
fi

# What Sentry holds for these pages: the same index.html, its Sourcemap header,
# and the map beside it under the same build.
held=$(held_files)
for page in agent home; do
    file=$(page_html $page)
    [ -f "$file" ] || { echo "::error::$file does not exist."; exit 1; }
    sha=$(sha1_of "$file")
    build=$(printf '%s\n' "$held" | awk -F'\t' -v n="app:///$page/index.html" -v s="$sha" '$1==n && $3==s && $4=="index.html.map" {print $2; exit}')
    if [ -z "$build" ] || ! printf '%s\n' "$held" | awk -F'\t' -v n="app:///$page/index.html.map" -v d="$build" '$1==n && $2==d {f=1} END {exit !f}'; then
        echo "::error::Sentry holds no source map for this $page page ($file) in release \"$release\", so its page error reports would not name the page's code."
        exit 1
    fi
    echo "Sentry holds the $page page's source map (release \"$release\", build $build)."
done

# to exercise the Link cursor), upload a file (409 when name+dist is taken).
import cgi, hashlib, json, sys
from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, HTTPServer
files = []
class H(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    def log_message(self, *a): sys.stderr.write("%s %s\n" % (self.command, self.path))
    def send(self, code, body, extra=None):
        data = json.dumps(body).encode()
        self.send_response(code); self.send_header("Content-Type", "application/json")
        for k, v in (extra or {}).items(): self.send_header(k, v)
        self.end_headers(); self.wfile.write(data)
    def do_GET(self):
        cursor = int(self.path.split("cursor=")[1]) if "cursor=" in self.path else 0
        page = files[cursor:cursor + 1]
        more = cursor + 1 < len(files)
        link = '<x>; rel="next"; results="%s"; cursor="%d"' % ("true" if more else "false", cursor + 1)
        self.send(200, page, {"Link": link})
    def do_POST(self):
        if self.path.endswith("/releases/"):
            self.rfile.read(int(self.headers["Content-Length"])); return self.send(208, {})
        form = cgi.FieldStorage(fp=self.rfile, headers=self.headers, environ={"REQUEST_METHOD": "POST"})
        name, dist = form.getvalue("name"), form.getvalue("dist")
        if any(f["name"] == name and f["dist"] == dist for f in files): return self.send(409, {"detail": "exists"})
        data = form["file"].file.read()
        hdrs = {}
        for h in (form.getlist("header") or []):
            k, v = h.split(":", 1); hdrs[k] = v.strip()
        files.append({"name": name, "dist": dist, "sha1": hashlib.sha1(data).hexdigest(), "headers": hdrs, "size": len(data)})
        self.send(201, files[-1])
HTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", int(sys.argv[1])), H).serve_forever()
EOF

I fixed all three stack gaps in the `errors-straight-to-sentry` worktree, nothing committed or pushed, and proved each on this Mac with the local stand-in. Nothing went to the real Sentry. While testing I found that most uncaught page errors never reach Sentry at all, which needs Kenneth's call (below).

**1. Reports show where the failure was thrown.**
- Boost 1.84 can't capture a throw's stack (that arrived in 1.85), and Sentry's SDK doesn't either. So the new `Support/ThrowStack` records every C++ throw: by overriding `__cxa_throw` on Mac and Linux, and with an exception handler on Windows.
- A failure that arrives as a value, such as an HTTP 500, has no throw. For those it records the stack of the code that found it, before reporting moves to the main thread and loses it.
- What it can't see: throws inside the Mac's system C++ library. On Windows it takes the reporting thread's latest throw.
- Trial: a malformed page message throws a few calls deep. Named with `atos`, the stack starts at `nlohmann::basic_json::at`, then `HomeHost::on_page_message`.

**2. File and line in Mac and Linux release builds.**
- The release workflow now builds with `-gline-tables-only` (line tables only, the smallest debug info that still gives file and line).
- Mac runs `dsymutil` and then `strip -S`. Linux checks the binary has a build id, then splits the debug info off with `objcopy`. Windows already ships full PDBs.
- `sentry_debug_files.sh verify` now fails unless Sentry holds debug info with file and line for each build id.
- I did a release-style Mac build with Apple's own `ar`. The largest archive is 544 MB (192 MB without line tables), far under the 4 GiB limit. The shipped binary is unchanged in size (176.8 MB) and the dSYM is 386 MB.
- A recorded event resolved from that dSYM to `LaunchReport.cpp:45` and `Http.cpp:537`.

**3. Page source maps.**
- Sentry 23.1.1 matches maps by file name and release only. Each page's frames are now renamed to `app:///home/index.html` (or `agent`) using Sentry's own `rewriteFramesIntegration`, so the name doesn't depend on where the app is installed.
- Each page also carries the commit as Sentry's `dist`, so a nightly can't overwrite a release's map.
- The build writes `<Page>UI/dist/index.html.map`, whose positions match the inlined `index.html`. That folder doesn't ship.
- The new `sentry_page_maps.sh upload|verify` runs in every platform's build and fails if a map is missing or a platform's page differs.
- Proof: the map resolved a real page error's top frame to `HomeUI/src/state/store.ts:122`, the exact null access.

Tests and checks:
- `jusprin_tests` (192 cases) and `agent_bridge_tests` (612) pass. AgentUI's 834 tests and HomeUI's 168 pass, and both type-check.
- clang-tidy passes on 25 files, shellcheck and actionlint are clean, and the new tests fail when their fix is taken out.
- The release skill and AGENTS.md "Releasing" are updated.

Not verified:
- Windows and Linux builds of all of this.
- The real upload, and Sentry actually applying the files.
- That the `dist` survives into the sent event.
- The page-map script ran only against a fake of Sentry's API.

**Decision needed: page errors that never reach Sentry.** The pages load from `file://`. In WKWebView an uncaught error there shows up only as "Script error." with no stack, and Sentry's default filters drop those. I checked this with a minimal WKWebView test app. So a crash while React draws the page, or in code the app calls in the page, sends nothing today; errors in the page's own timers and listeners do arrive. I expect the earlier hand-made catcher had the same gap, but haven't checked. Options:
- **(a)** Load the pages from a custom URL scheme. I expect full error details then, but haven't tested it, and it changes how both pages load.
- **(b)** Add a React error boundary plus a catch where the app calls into the page. It covers less and changes what the person sees when the page fails.
- **(c)** Leave it.

My pick is (a). Should I prototype it?

The new `build-lines/arm64` folder (2.4 GB) is left in the worktree. Notes are in the shared `errors-straight-to-sentry.md`.
Prototype the custom URL scheme

# Fork stewardship

**Status:** Required discipline for every change to an upstream-owned file on `jusprin-dev`.

JusPrin is a long-lived fork. Every line it changes in an OrcaSlicer-owned file is a line it re-resolves at every rebase, forever, by a person who was not there when the line was written. The rules below exist to keep that permanent cost small and, where it cannot be small, to keep it visible.

One question generates all of them: **after this change, what does the fork own?**

- Owning *product policy* is safe. It is ours, upstream will never write it, and it lives in our files.
- Owning a *small neutral seam* is acceptable. It is the kind of thing upstream might plausibly have written itself, so it survives refactors and could be contributed back.
- Owning *upstream's behavior* is the expensive kind. It commits us to re-deriving upstream's intent forever, and the day we take ownership is usually the day the behavior quietly diverges.

Two mechanical facts drive everything else. Git merges text, not meaning: it conflicts when two sides touch the same or adjacent lines, and it stays silent when they touch different lines even if the result is nonsense. And a conflict is a *stop* — a human is forced to look — while silent divergence is unbounded and invisible. Conflicts are therefore not the enemy. Unnoticed drift is, and conflicts that resolve wrongly are.

## The ten principles

### 1. Conflict probability is about where you write, not how much

**Rule.** Place fork edits where upstream rarely writes, and keep the number of distinct sites low.

**Mechanism.** Risk is roughly *how often upstream edits this region* times *how much of the region you occupy*, summed over every place you touched. Each site is an independent draw. New files have probability zero, so their size is free; one line inside a function upstream is actively reworking is expensive.

**The test.** How many separate places does this change touch, and how busy is each one? Would one seam deliver the same capability?

**Violation.** Delivering a single capability through a dozen scattered notification lines across several upstream files, when one funnel that every path already passes through would have carried them.

### 2. A clean merge is not a safe merge

**Rule.** Prefer edits that are locally correct over edits that participate in upstream's control flow.

**Mechanism.** Git merges text. If your edit's correctness depends on the code around it — an ordering, a guard, an early return, an invariant nobody wrote down — upstream can restructure the surroundings, the merge succeeds, and your edit now runs under assumptions that no longer hold, with no signal at all.

**The test.** If upstream restructures the code around this hunk, do I get a conflict or silence? If silence, would any test catch it?

**Violation.** Moving a member out of a constructor's initializer list because a callback can fire mid-construction. Nothing in upstream's code records that invariant, so a future cleanup restores the old form with no conflict and no error.

### 3. Add to upstream's code; do not revise it

**Rule.** Append, insert, and call. Do not rewrite upstream functions or change their signatures.

**Mechanism.** An additive hook fails gracefully: when it conflicts, the resolution is "keep both," and anyone can do that correctly. A rewritten function fails badly: every future upstream change to it is a conflict whose resolution requires re-deriving two intents at once, in code no longer shared with upstream. Rewriting subtle logic also tends to change it, and you find out later.

**The test.** Does upstream's line survive my change? If I deleted or replaced one, why could I not have added next to it?

**Violation.** Replacing OrcaSlicer's undo and redo implementations with fork-owned equivalents in order to learn whether the history position moved. Re-expressing the vendor-specific snapshot walk silently dropped one of its branches. An additive helper that reports the result, leaving upstream's functions untouched, would have answered the same question.

### 4. Own the policy; borrow the mechanism

**Rule.** No product name, color, dimension, or product-specific decision in an upstream-owned file. Upstream files may gain small neutral capabilities; the policy that uses them lives in fork-owned code.

**Mechanism.** Product specifics in upstream files are permanent divergence: they can never be upstreamed and never dropped, so they must be re-resolved forever. A neutral capability — a flag, a getter/setter pair, an event — reads like something upstream could have written, which is exactly why it survives refactors.

**The test.** Would this addition look reasonable in an upstream pull request, with no explanation of our product?

**Violation.** A product-named enum value inside a rendering class, or product decisions embedded in an upstream mouse handler. The fix is a neutral options struct plus a fork-owned controller that applies our policy.

### 5. One seam beats many touch points

**Rule.** Find the single place every path already passes through, and put the fork's line there.

**Mechanism.** Each touch point is an independent conflict draw and an independent thing a future resolver must understand. Collapsing many small recurring costs into one is worth some indirection.

**The test.** Do all the paths I am hooking already converge somewhere downstream? Is there one function that runs exactly when the thing I care about has happened?

**Violation.** Publishing a history-changed event from undo, from redo, and from both history-navigation entry points, when all four funnel through a single update function that runs only on a successful move.

### 6. One shared implementation is worth a guaranteed conflict

**Rule.** When the alternative is two copies of the same behavior, keep the shared path and accept that it will conflict.

**Mechanism.** A conflict is a stop; drift between two copies is silent and unbounded. Trading an invisible risk for a visible, small, recurring one is a good trade.

**The test.** Where did the logic I removed actually go? A move has one implementation; only a duplication risks divergence. If I wrote new behavior beside an existing upstream path rather than calling it, upstream's future improvements will never reach our users.

**Violation.** Writing a second object-duplication routine next to OrcaSlicer's clipboard path and pointing an existing dialog at it. Reusing the existing path — extending it where it was too narrow — keeps one implementation.

### 7. Unavoidable conflicts must be easy to resolve correctly

**Rule.** When you must delete or relocate an upstream line, say at the site what moved, where it went, and what a future rebase must carry across.

**Mechanism.** The real cost of a conflict is not the stop; it is the chance of resolving it wrongly. Appending near an upstream line yields a conflict whose obvious resolution — keep both — is right. Deleting an upstream line yields a conflict whose obvious resolution — take mine, the logic moved — silently discards whatever upstream did to that line in the meantime.

**The test.** Six months from now, is the natural resolution of the conflict I am creating the correct one? If not, what does the resolver need to read to get it right, and is that text next to the conflict?

**Violation.** Removing an upstream snapshot label that upstream later localized. Git stops for a human, but the intent-faithful resolution throws the translation away, and nothing at the site says otherwise.

### 8. Do not diverge where you gain nothing; converge where upstream already went

**Rule.** No gratuitous formatting, reordering, or whitespace differences. Before reverting a cosmetic difference, compare against current upstream — it may have made the same change.

**Mechanism.** Every valueless difference is a conflict site that buys nothing. And if upstream has independently arrived at your version, "fixing" it back creates divergence rather than removing it. Adopting a change upstream has already made converges the two trees early and makes the eventual conflict resolve itself.

**The test.** Does this difference carry meaning? Has upstream already made it?

**Violation.** Consuming a shared blank line in a list of build subdirectories, where upstream also appends entries.

### 9. Verify the risk claim instead of reasoning about it

**Rule.** Before asserting that a change is or is not rebase-risky, check it. Three checks, each one command: does git actually conflict there; has upstream already converged on the same change; is the change a move or a duplication.

**Mechanism.** A coherent story about fork risk is not a true one, and every one of these is cheaper to check than to argue about. Reasoning alone reliably produces confident, wrong claims — that a lost change is "silent" when git stops for it, that a move is a "duplication," that a cosmetic difference is gratuitous when upstream shares it.

**The test.** Did I run the simulation, or am I describing what I expect it to say?

**Violation.** A report that lists which files are rebase-sensitive and calls the change narrow, without having run the merge simulation that would have found two lossy resolutions waiting in it.

### 10. Take each upstream release by merging from the release we last took

**Rule.** Take a new upstream release with a merge whose base is the upstream release the fork last took. Never run a plain `git merge` of upstream, and never rewrite the fork's history to take a release.

**Mechanism.** The fork follows upstream's release branches, and each release branch splits off upstream's development line on its own. A plain merge picks the common ancestor itself, a development-line commit from before both release branches. Its conflict list is then everything that differs between the two release branches: vendor profiles, translations, CI files, none of it ours. Naming the last release we took as the base limits the merge to the fork's own changes. That gives the same conflicts a replay would hit, resolved once, with no commits rewritten, so branches in progress merge forward without a rebase. Measured on 2026-11-07, going from v2.4.2 to v2.5.0: 22 conflicted files either way, and a branch in progress merged into the trial result with no conflicts.

**How.** In a worktree on a new branch from `jusprin-dev`, the development branch:

```bash
git rev-parse <new release>^{commit} > "$(git rev-parse --git-dir)/MERGE_HEAD"
git merge-recursive <last release taken> -- HEAD <new release>
```

Resolve the conflicts, then `git commit`. A later patch release on the same release branch, such as 2.5.1 after 2.5.0, needs no override: a plain `git merge` finds the right base.

**The test.** Is the merge base the release we last took, and not a commit on upstream's development line?

**Violation.** `git merge upstream/main` or `git merge v2.5.0` with no base given. Each produces thousands of conflicts in files JusPrin never edited.

## Before you finish

A change that touches upstream-owned files is not done until this is recorded in the handback or pull request:

1. **The rebase simulation and its result.** Run it against the newest upstream release, with the release the fork last took as the base (rule 10), and name both endpoint commits — measurements are not reproducible otherwise.

   ```bash
   git merge-tree --write-tree --merge-base=<last release taken> <newest upstream release> HEAD
   ```

   For each conflicted file, state whether the natural resolution is correct or lossy. A lossy one is a defect to fix now, not a note for later.

2. **An account of every upstream line deleted or rewritten.** Where the logic went, and why an additive form was not possible.

3. **A statement of what the fork now owns.** Policy, a neutral seam, or upstream behavior. The third needs an explicit justification.

An automatic merge is evidence about today's text. It is not proof that a future rebase will merge, and never proof that the merged result behaves correctly. After every upstream update, run the focused contract tests, the full native build, the real multi-plate workflow, native gizmo input, and the stock-behavior regression checks.

## This fork's terrain

Facts specific to OrcaSlicer, worth knowing before choosing where to put a seam. They change over time; re-measure rather than trusting these.

`Plater.cpp` is by far the busiest file the fork touches, followed by the central `src/slic3r/CMakeLists.txt`, `GLCanvas3D.cpp`, and `PartPlate.cpp`. `GLToolbar` and `GLGizmosManager` are quiet. File-level churn is only a first approximation: some functions inside `Plater.cpp` have not been touched upstream in the entire life of this fork, and a seam there is far cheaper than the file's overall rate suggests. Measure the function, not just the file.

Some native state is shared rather than owned by one object. OrcaSlicer's collapse toolbar belongs to `Plater` and is used by both the Prepare and Preview canvases, so a per-canvas guard cannot save and restore it correctly. Shared state needs one owner at the shared lifetime boundary, and exact restoration needs a getter as well as a setter.

`MainFrame`'s Notebook is cheaper to wrap than to dismantle. Dozens of
upstream predicates — menu and shortcut enabling, `can_delete`, slice status
updates, undo/redo gating — key off `m_tabpanel->GetSelection()`, so removing
or reparenting the Prepare/Preview pages breaks them with no conflict and no
error. A shell gets a tabless full-window layout for free instead: hide the
strip via the public `GetBtnsListCtrl()` (wxBookCtrlBase gives a hidden
controller zero size, so pages fill the client area), and the stock slice and
print side buttons disappear with it because `ButtonsListCtrl` reparents them
into the strip at construction. The Phase 1 production shell reached a
19-added-line upstream footprint this way where the POC's reparenting shell
needed edits across eight upstream files.

The same measurement gives the rule for every fork-owned screen that comes
after the shell. OrcaSlicer's surfaces (the stock homepage, Prepare, Preview,
Monitor, the settings tabs) stay inside the Notebook, because their
correctness depends on it. Fork-owned surfaces (the header, the Agent pane,
Home, and whatever follows) live outside it, as siblings of the Notebook in a
fork-owned sizer, shown and hidden by the shell. The shell *reads* the
Notebook's selection to decide what to show and *never edits its page list*:
no `RemovePage`, `InsertPage`, or reparenting of a stock page. Removing or
replacing a page hands the fork the meaning of that index. Upstream keeps
addressing it by number — `tpHome` as a dialog parent, the target of
`EVT_LOAD_URL`, the tab `post_init` returns to — and every one of those lands
on the fork's widget with no conflict and no error. If a fork surface truly
must be a page, append it last, where no upstream code addresses it.

Navigation between screens stays a Notebook selection change even when the
screen being left is fork-owned. Menu and shortcut enabling, undo and redo
availability, and slice-status updates all read `GetSelection()`, so the
selection must remain the one record of which OrcaSlicer surface is active.
Showing Prepare any other way leaves those predicates answering for the wrong
page, silently.

Some stock behavior is already exposed as an event idiom rather than a
function. Upstream itself drives plate slicing from two places with the same
sequence — the slice button and the Cmd+R shortcut both run
`plater->update(true, true)`, post `EVT_GLTOOLBAR_SLICE_PLATE` to the Plater,
and select the Preview tab — so fork code may repeat that short dispatch
without violating the shared-implementation rule; the behavior itself stays
owned by Plater's event handler.

Historical measurements and the incidents behind several of these rules are in the [OrcaSlicer integration guide](orca-integration-guide.md) and, for the spike era, in the [POC reference](poc-reference.md).

content.text:
On macOS, uncaught errors in the Home and AI pages now reach Sentry in full. Both pages now load from `jusprin:///home/index.html` and `jusprin:///agent/index.html` instead of a `file://` address. Under `file://`, Mac's web view gives only "Script error." for these errors, and Sentry drops that. Nothing is committed.

**What I changed** (all in the `errors-straight-to-sentry` worktree)
- **A file lookup.** `Support/PageFiles` finds the file a `jusprin:///` address names inside `resources/jusprin`. It refuses `..`, `.`, empty path parts, backslashes, folders and missing files.
- **The page address and its handler.** `Support/PageScheme` gives each page's address: `jusprin:///` on macOS, and the old `file://` address on Windows and Linux. It also gives the handler that serves those files.
- **The two callers.** `HomeWebView.cpp` and `AgentWebView.cpp` use that address and pass the handler on.
- **One seam in Orca's `Widgets/WebView`.** There is a new `CreateWebView(parent, url, handlers)`. The old two-argument version forwards to it with no handlers. No upstream line is deleted.

**What I tested**
- **Same error, both addresses.** In the scratch app I added one error to the Home page, thrown 6 seconds after it loads:
  - Over `file://`, nothing reached the stand-in for Sentry.
  - Over `jusprin:///`, the full error arrived: the message, the function `homeTrialThrow`, and the frame `app:///home/index.html` at line 77, column 88.
  - The event's history shows both Home and the AI page finished their handshake with the app.
- **What still works.** In a small test harness, a custom-scheme page counts as a secure page, page storage works, and the printer camera picture (`http://`) still loads.
- **Unit tests.** All 195 JusPrin unit tests pass, including 3 new ones for the file lookup.
- **Include check.** The include check CI runs passes on the 27 changed files.
- **Rebase simulation**, from OrcaSlicer 2.5.0 to 2.5.1 (`eef7710cb1`) and to upstream `main` (`07f38df2a4`):
  - The two `WebView` files merge cleanly.
  - The four files that conflict (`OrcaSlicer.cpp`, `ProjectStrategy.hpp`, `Plater.cpp`, `Plater.hpp`) conflict the same way without my change.

**What the person now sees.** On Mac, page errors that used to vanish now show the generic "Something went wrong on our side" message with a way to report it. That is what the error-handling rules ask for every unexpected error, but people will see it more often.

**Still open**
- **Dropping a file onto a page.** If the page doesn't catch the drop, the app opens the file only when the web view starts loading the file's `file://` address. Whether Mac's web view still does that from a `jusprin:///` page is untested; it needs a real mouse drag.
- **Windows and Linux.** They still load from `file://`. It's untested whether their web views also hide these errors.
  - Linux can't just reuse the Mac code. There, wx registers a scheme once for the whole app and ties it to the first web view that registered it, so closing that view would leave the scheme pointing at freed memory.

Details are in `errors-straight-to-sentry.md` in the shared notes folder, under "Pages on a custom URL scheme".

The search turned up no official Microsoft documentation for `__current_exception` itself. The results are mostly third-party source code and mailing-list threads, which together show how the function is used.

- **Signature:** Boost's stacktrace code declares it as `extern "C" void** __cdecl __current_exception()` and notes it comes from vcruntime.dll exported from vcruntime.dll. LibreOffice's bridge code uses the same declaration. Its comments point to the per-thread data structure, where a current-exception slot is kept is defined in MSVS14.0/VC/crt/src/vcruntime/frame.cpp.
- **Exception record:** Boost dereferences the returned pointer and casts the result to `PEXCEPTION_RECORD`, so the function gives back a pointer to the in-flight exception's record. Microsoft's docs say that an exception is represented by an EXCEPTION_RECORD structure in its implementation.
- **excptptr.cpp:** Microsoft's STL `excptptr.cpp` is the source for `exception_ptr`. A libc++ patch copies it verbatim from a 2024-06-10 snapshot of microsoft/STL's main branch. Its header comment says it communicates with the EH runtime though vcruntime's per-thread-data structure. A GitHub gist also hosts a copy of the file, with the copyright header and a "exception_ptr implementation" description.
- **Wine usage:** Wine's msvcrt code calls `__current_exception()` to read the current `EXCEPTION_RECORD` when it builds an `exception_ptr`, falling back to NULL when none exists (Wine commit threads, items 14 and 17).

content.text: Boost's own throw-stack code uses `__current_exception()` on Windows, which is a strong precedent. I'm reading how it matches a throw to the exception being handled.

input.prompt: Show verbatim the Windows (_MSC_VER) part and the POSIX part: how a throw's stack is stored and how current_exception_stacktrace finds the stack of the exception being handled (what key, how it avoids matching a different exception, any refcount or exception_ptr handling, any __cxa_begin_catch or __cxa_allocate_exception hooks).

result.output:
I can't show the Windows and POSIX sections verbatim because they're too long to quote within the 125-character limit per quote. Here is a concise summary of how each path works.

**Windows (`_MSC_VER` / MinGW)**

- **Capture:** A vectored exception handler, installed at static initialization, watches for MSVC C++ exception records. When it sees a throw that isn't a rethrow, it grows a thread-local array of entries and records the thrown object's address as the key. It then writes a 4096-byte stack dump, skipping 4 frames, into that entry.
- **Rethrow detection:** A throw is treated as a rethrow if its object address is zero or matches the currently active C++ exception. Rethrows don't create new dumps.
- **Lookup:** `boost_stacktrace_impl_current_exception_stacktrace` gets the active exception record from the VC runtime, then searches the array from newest to oldest for a matching object address. It returns that dump, or null if none matches.
- **Ownership:** The dumps and array are freed in the thread-local data's destructor. There is no refcount handling, no `exception_ptr` handling, and no `__cxa_*` hook on this path.

**POSIX (non-MSVC)**

- **Capture hook:** `__cxa_allocate_exception` is overridden and forwards to the real function via `dlsym(RTLD_NEXT)`. When capture is enabled, it rounds the thrown size up to max alignment, allocates an extra 4096 bytes, and writes a stack dump (skipping 1 frame) directly after the thrown object.
- **Storage with the libstdc++/GCC ABI:** The dump pointer is stored in the reserved padding of the exception header. The code asserts that this padding was zeroed beforehand.
- **Storage with libc++:** The runtime is detected through a weak symbol. Unless `BOOST_STACKTRACE_ALWAYS_STORE_IN_PADDING` is set, the dump pointer is stored in a mutex-guarded map keyed by the exception object's address.
- **Lookup:** `current_exception_stacktrace` returns null if capture is disabled. Otherwise it calls `std::current_exception()` and extracts the raw exception object pointer from it. That pointer is the key, either into the map or into the padding. Matching is by object identity, so it refers to the exception actually being handled.
- **Refcounting (libc++ only):** `__cxa_decrement_exception_refcount` is overridden. When the refcount is 1, the map entry is erased before the original function runs. The code notes a race that can cause a false positive or a leak.
- **Leak guard:** Concurrent throws on libc++ may leak. The program aborts with a warning unless `BOOST_STACKTRACE_LIBCXX_RUNTIME_MAY_CAUSE_MEMORY_LEAK=1` is set, or the library was built with the matching macro defined.
- **`__cxa_begin_catch`:** No hook for it appears in this code.
- **Debug guard:** In non-NDEBUG builds, a thread-local counter guards `__cxa_allocate_exception` against runaway recursion.
- **Cleanup check:** `assert_no_pending_traces` asserts that the libc++ map is empty.

I fixed both problems. A report no longer gets an earlier throw's stack, and the pages now build byte for byte the same with Windows line endings. Everything is tested on Mac, except the Windows C++ change, which I couldn't compile here. Nothing is committed.

**1. Wrong throw stack**

- **Reproduced:** with your program and with a new test in `tests/jusprin/test_throw_stack.cpp`. The test failed on the old code: `std::stoi` and `std::string::at` errors got the earlier app throw's frames.
- **Fix on macOS and Linux:** the app now also has its own `__cxa_begin_catch`, which runs at every catch in the app's code. The first time the app catches a recorded exception, the record keeps a hold on that exception. While it holds it, the runtime can't give its address to another exception. A lookup accepts only a record holding the exception being handled; anything else falls back to the reporting code's stack.
  - The test now passes.
  - Your program now shows 0 frames for `stoi` and `string::at`, while the app's own throw keeps its 3.
  - A second new test checks that an exception stored and rethrown later still finds its own throw. That is the path the AI page's host uses.
- **Cost:** an exception the app caught stays alive until 32 newer throws have been recorded, so its destructor runs later than before.
- **One case can still name the wrong throw:**
  1. The app throws an exception that only code outside the app ever catches, for example the C++ library's stream code swallowing a failure from one of the app's streams.
  2. That exception is freed.
  3. A throw the app can't see then reuses its address, and the app catches it.

  I found no way to close this on macOS without reaching into the C++ runtime's private data.
- **Windows:** the old code took the latest throw on the thread without comparing anything. It now keeps the thread's recent throws keyed by the thrown object, skips rethrows, and finds the exception being handled through `__current_exception()`, as Boost.Stacktrace does on Windows. This part has not been compiled or run.

**2. Page-map step on Windows**

- **Measured:** I checked the page folders out twice with git, once with `core.autocrlf=true` as the Windows runner does, and once with it off.
  - With it on, 306 files got CRLF.
  - The AI page came out different, and so did both pages' source maps. The upload compares the maps too, so both pages would have failed.
- **Fix:** make the pages build the same everywhere, which was smaller than keeping one map per platform. New `.gitattributes` files in `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin` (covering `AgentUI`, `HomeUI`, `WebShared` and `Localization`), `resources/jusprin` and `docs/guide` keep those files LF on every checkout. No upstream file changed.
- **Result:** with the rules, the Windows-style checkout builds both pages and both maps byte for byte the same as the Mac and Linux one.

**Checks run:**
- The JusPrin unit tests (197 cases), the AI-bridge tests (612) and the AI page (834) and Home page (168) tests pass.
- The include check passes.
- The scratch copy of the app ran normally, and its start-report HTTP 500 still arrived as an error report.

Sources:

=== linux-arm-docker-build
---
name: linux-arm-docker-build
description: JusPrin/OrcaSlicer deps build cleanly on ARM Linux in Docker on the Mac; recipe, gotchas, and the GUI-testing path.
metadata:
  type: project
---

All 25 OrcaSlicer dependencies compile on aarch64 Linux — verified 2026-09-07,
45 minutes wall clock, exit 0, artifacts confirmed `ELF 64-bit ARM aarch64`.
No arch-specific patches were needed.

**Do not write a new Dockerfile.** `build_linux.sh -g` already embeds one
(function `docker_runner_dockerfile`, Ubuntu 24.04, and it already branches on
`aarch64|arm64` for the CMake download). Extract it or use `-g` directly.

Recipe that worked:
- Image: `orca-linux-builder:arm64`, built from that embedded Dockerfile with a
  minimal context (only `build_linux.sh` + `scripts/linux.d` are COPYed).
- Workspace: Docker **named volume** `orca-work`, populated with
  `git archive HEAD | docker run -i -v orca-work:/work ... tar -x`.
  Never bind-mount the repo: `build_linux.sh` does `sed --in-place` on
  `version.inc` and writes Linux artifacts into `deps/build/` next to the
  macOS `deps/build/arm64`. VirtioFS bind mounts are also slow for builds.
- Run: `./build_linux.sh -dr -j 6` with `--memory=10g` so the build cannot
  starve the ~18 other containers on this machine.

Gotchas hit, in order:
1. `github.com/.../archive/refs/tags/*.zip` returns **504** intermittently and
   CMake caches the zero-byte result. The Mac host got the same 504, so it is
   GitHub, not the container. Fix: fetch from `codeload.github.com/<org>/<repo>/zip/refs/tags/<tag>`
   and drop it into `deps/DL_CACHE/<Dep>/<file>`; the hash check then passes.
2. `cc1plus` OOM-killed during OpenVDB. Docker Desktop was set to **4 GB**
   while OrcaSlicer's own script demands 10 GB. Raised to 16 GB (settings-store.json
   and settings.json, keys `MemoryMiB`/`memoryMiB`, then restart Docker Desktop).
3. After a Docker Desktop restart, 8 of 18 containers have restart policy `no`
   (the whole `prind-*` Klipper stack, `tsd-enterprise-db-1` Postgres,
   `tsd-enterprise-object_store-1`) and must be `docker start`ed by hand.
   Snapshot `docker ps` before restarting Docker.
4. `| tee` masks the build exit code — use `set -o pipefail`.

GUI testing on top of this: Xvfb + Mesa `llvmpipe` gives **OpenGL 4.5** inside
the container, enough for the 3D plater canvas. Capture with ImageMagick
`import -window root` into a shared dir and read the PNG. `xdotool` for input.
Software rendering, so it is not a faithful check of GPU-specific behavior.
See [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]] for the native macOS path.
=== windows-build-on-gcp-vm
---
name: windows-build-on-gcp-vm
description: JusPrin builds and runs on the GCP Windows VM; the five traps that make it fail, and why the CI Windows job failing is a runner-environment problem, not a script bug.
metadata:
  type: project
---

JusPrin compiles from source on the Windows test VM and the built binary runs
with its Agent UI visible. Verified 2026-09-07 on n2-standard-16: deps 22.7 min,
slicer 23.0 min. Output is `orca-slicer.exe` (261 KB launcher) plus
`OrcaSlicer.dll` (122.7 MB). Full recipe in
`/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/.claude/vm-harness/windows/BUILDING.md`; VM setup in its README.
See [[windows-gui-test-vm-gcp]].

**Why:** four of the five failures below produce misleading errors far from
their cause, and two were self-inflicted by how the build was driven.

**How to apply:**
- Run long builds as a Windows **scheduled task** (SYSTEM / ServiceAccount), not
  over SSH — OpenSSH kills the process tree on disconnect. Never let two builds
  share a directory: that produced OpenSSL `C1033 cannot open program database`.
- Add `C:\Program Files\Git\usr\bin` to PATH so **awk** is found, or libpng
  cannot generate `pngprefix.h` (`-DPNG_PREFIX=` in deps/PNG/PNG.cmake) and you
  get a confusing `C1083` on a header that was never written.
- Set `CMAKE_POLICY_VERSION_MINIMUM=3.5` for CMake 4.x.
- **Do not use the CI deps artifact** — the shipped bundle predates `deps/Eigen`
  and cannot satisfy Eigen 5.0.1. Build deps from source.
- Never hard-stop the VM mid-build: doing so left 622 installed files full of
  NUL bytes and surfaced as fake syntax errors inside Boost headers.
- Qhull is deliberately excluded on MSVC (deps/CMakeLists.txt), so 24/25 is
  complete on Windows.
- To run headless, use the app's own hook rather than dropping DLLs beside the
  exe: `src/OrcaSlicer_app_msvc.cpp` loads `<exedir>\mesa\opengl32.dll` when
  system OpenGL < 2.0. Still force `GALLIUM_DRIVER=llvmpipe`.

The `Build all` Windows CI job fails at `cmake -G "Visual Studio 17 2022"` with
"could not find any instance of Visual Studio". That is a GitHub runner
environment problem, not `build_release_vs.bat` — the same script selects the
same generator on the VM and configures fine against registered Build Tools.

**MSVC rejects `this` in a nested lambda's init-capture.** Found 2026-09-07 at
commit fbe5963b: `CallAfter([self=wxWeakRef<wxWindow>(this),...])` written INSIDE
another lambda compiled on clang but failed on MSVC with 37 errors, because MSVC
bound that `this` to the enclosing closure object, so it tried to build a
`wxWeakRef<wxWindow>` from a lambda pointer
(`Tracked_class_should_inherit_from_wxTrackable`). Name the object first —
`auto* menu = this;` then capture `menu`. Watch for this pattern whenever a
deferred callback is set up from within another lambda; it is invisible on macOS.

**PowerShell splits `-m:6` (2026-10-24).** In a .ps1, `& cmake --build … -- -m:6 -v:m`
reaches MSBuild as `-m:` `6` and fails at once ("For switch syntax, type
MSBuild -help"). Quote them: `'-m:6' '-v:m'`. Also `*>>` writes UTF-16, so
Select-String on that log matches nothing; use `2>&1 | Out-File -Encoding utf8`.
A watcher built from `winssh.sh 'powershell -Command "…\"…\"…"'` silently never
matched for 3 hours — the quoting rule above applies to status checks too.
Killing "my" processes by command-line match also took out a taskhostw.exe;
kill the PIDs your own task started (and their /T trees), not a pattern.

**Shell harness on the VM (2026-11-07, app-menus).** `C:\src\JusPrin\build\tests\shell\Release\shell_integration_harness.exe` has Mesa beside it; run it from a .cmd with `GALLIUM_DRIVER=llvmpipe` and `LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE=1` through an Interactive scheduled task as guitest; it uses its own temp data dir. Build it with `cmake --build build --config Release --target jusprin_web shell_integration_harness -- '-m:12'` (node is at `C:\Users\guitest\.local\node-v24.21.0-win-x64`). The VM has no access to unpushed commits: send them with `git bundle create f.bundle <branch> ^<vm-head>`.
- MSVC also rejects a local `constexpr` used inside a lambda that doesn't capture it (C3493; clang accepts). Make it `static constexpr`.
- On jusprin-newui b0a2fe3b08 the default suite already fails 6 checks on Windows: three failed_autosave_* checks (the harness simulates a failed save by removing write permission, and Windows ignores that on folders), earlier_model_version_available, and agent_panel_columns_tile_the_client at 1000 and 1400 DIP. Compare against that list before blaming a change.
- In PowerShell, `[IO.File]` takes relative paths from the process folder, not from Set-Location; use absolute paths. In a .cmd, `echo exit=%ERRORLEVEL%>> f` turns `0>>` into a redirect; put a space before `>>`.
